Skin releases and champion balance: general overview

Construction and exploration of the first analysis cohort

Objective

The main hypothesis is that champions receive buffs shortly before a skin is released, potentially to increase skin sales. A secondary question is whether this pattern is stronger for champions that are already popular.

This first report constructs one row per non-base skin release. It is descriptive: because every row is a skin release, it cannot by itself establish whether buffs are more common than during comparable periods without a skin release. A later modelling step should add champion-specific control dates and account for repeated releases for the same champion.

The analysis uses the following conventions:

  • skin releases before 2011 are excluded;
  • skins marked as cancelled and skins without a release date are excluded;
  • skins released from the champion’s release date through 60 days afterward are excluded;
  • performance is linearly interpolated 30 days before and 14 days after the release date;
  • buffs are counted from 42 days before through the release date, including changes shipped on the release date;
  • nerfs are counted from the day after release through 42 days after release;
  • only buffs and nerfs classified as CERTAIN or VERY_CERTAIN are counted;
  • a skin is excluded if the champion has any classified rework within 60 days on either side of its release;
  • multiple skins for the same champion on the same date remain separate rows because the unit is a skin release.

The graph source contains dates but no release times. Interpolation therefore evaluates each target date at midnight UTC.

Setup

This report deliberately uses data.table and base R graphics rather than the tidyverse.

Install the three required packages once before rendering:

install.packages(c("DBI", "RSQLite", "data.table"))
Code 
required_packages <- c("DBI", "RSQLite", "data.table")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1L), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the required R packages first: ",
    paste(sprintf("install.packages('%s')", missing_packages), collapse = "; ")
  )
}

library(data.table)

locate_database <- function(configured_path = NULL) {
  candidates <- if (!is.null(configured_path) && nzchar(configured_path)) {
    configured_path
  } else {
    c(
      "data/lol_skin_release_statistics.sqlite3",
      "../../data/lol_skin_release_statistics.sqlite3"
    )
  }
  existing <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(existing) == 0L) {
    stop("SQLite database not found. Render from the repository root or set params.database.")
  }
  normalizePath(existing[[1L]], mustWork = TRUE)
}

database_path <- locate_database(params$database)
connection <- DBI::dbConnect(
  RSQLite::SQLite(),
  dbname = database_path,
  flags = RSQLite::SQLITE_RO
)

pre_performance_days <- 30L
post_performance_days <- 14L
balance_window_days <- 42L
rework_window_days <- 60L
champion_release_window_days <- 60L
accepted_confidence <- c("CERTAIN", "VERY_CERTAIN")

Read the normalized source tables

champion_id below is Riot’s stable numeric champion ID. skin_id is the Wiki/Riot skin ID rather than the SQLite surrogate key.

Code 
skins <- as.data.table(DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "
  SELECT
    champions.game_id AS champion_id,
    champions.name AS champion_name,
    skins.wiki_skin_id AS skin_id,
    skins.display_name AS skin_name,
    skins.release_date AS skin_release_date,
    base_skin.release_date AS champion_release_date
  FROM skins
  JOIN champions ON champions.id = skins.champion_id
  JOIN skins AS base_skin
    ON base_skin.champion_id = champions.id
   AND base_skin.is_base = 1
  WHERE skins.is_base = 0
    AND skins.release_date IS NOT NULL
    AND skins.release_date >= '2011-01-01'
    AND skins.availability <> 'Canceled'
  ORDER BY skins.release_date, champions.name, skins.wiki_skin_id
"))

graph_points <- as.data.table(DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "
  SELECT
    champions.game_id AS champion_id,
    graph_series.metric,
    graph_points.observed_at_ms,
    graph_points.value
  FROM graph_points
  JOIN graph_series ON graph_series.id = graph_points.graph_series_id
  JOIN champions ON champions.id = graph_series.champion_id
  WHERE graph_series.metric IN ('win_rate', 'popularity')
  ORDER BY champions.game_id, graph_series.metric, graph_points.observed_at_ms
"))

classified_changes <- as.data.table(DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "
  SELECT
    champions.game_id AS champion_id,
    patch_events.patch_id,
    patch_events.effective_date,
    classifications.label AS classification_label,
    classifications.confidence
  FROM classifications
  JOIN patch_entries ON patch_entries.id = classifications.patch_entry_id
  JOIN patch_events ON patch_events.id = patch_entries.patch_event_id
  JOIN champions ON champions.id = patch_events.champion_id
  WHERE classifications.label IN ('buff', 'nerf', 'rework')
"))

DBI::dbDisconnect(connection)

skins[, skin_release_date := as.IDate(skin_release_date)]
skins[, champion_release_date := as.IDate(champion_release_date)]
graph_points[, observed_at_ms := as.numeric(observed_at_ms)]
classified_changes[, effective_date := as.IDate(effective_date)]
classified_changes[, effective_day := as.integer(effective_date)]

Interpolate performance around each release

Linear interpolation uses only observations from the same champion and metric. Targets before the first or after the last available observation remain missing rather than being extrapolated.

Code 
graph_points[, series_key := paste(champion_id, metric, sep = "::")]
graph_series <- split(
  graph_points[, .(observed_at_ms, value)],
  graph_points$series_key
)

interpolate_value <- function(champion, metric_name, target_date) {
  series <- graph_series[[paste(champion, metric_name, sep = "::")]]
  if (is.null(series) || nrow(series) < 2L) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  target_ms <- as.numeric(target_date) * 86400000
  if (target_ms < series$observed_at_ms[[1L]] || target_ms > series$observed_at_ms[[nrow(series)]]) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  stats::approx(
    x = series$observed_at_ms,
    y = series$value,
    xout = target_ms,
    method = "linear",
    ties = "ordered",
    rule = 1L
  )$y
}

skin_windows <- copy(skins)
skin_windows[, win_rate_1m_before := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    interpolate_value(champion, "win_rate", release_date - pre_performance_days)
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, win_rate_2w_after := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    interpolate_value(champion, "win_rate", release_date + post_performance_days)
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, popularity_1m_before := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    interpolate_value(champion, "popularity", release_date - pre_performance_days)
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, popularity_2w_after := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    interpolate_value(champion, "popularity", release_date + post_performance_days)
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]

Count nearby balance changes

Counts refer to individually classified patch-history entries. Distinct patch counts are retained as diagnostics so that one patch containing several changes can be distinguished from several separate buff or nerf patches.

Code 
changes_by_champion <- split(classified_changes, classified_changes$champion_id)

count_changes <- function(champion, target_label, first_date, last_date, distinct_patches = FALSE) {
  changes <- changes_by_champion[[as.character(champion)]]
  if (is.null(changes)) {
    return(0L)
  }

  selected <- changes[
    classification_label == target_label &
      confidence %chin% accepted_confidence &
      !is.na(effective_day) &
      effective_day >= as.integer(first_date) &
      effective_day <= as.integer(last_date)
  ]
  if (distinct_patches) {
    return(uniqueN(selected$patch_id))
  }
  nrow(selected)
}

skin_windows[, buff_entries_6w_before := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    count_changes(
      champion,
      "buff",
      release_date - balance_window_days,
      release_date
    )
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, buff_patches_6w_before := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    count_changes(
      champion,
      "buff",
      release_date - balance_window_days,
      release_date,
      distinct_patches = TRUE
    )
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, nerf_entries_6w_after := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    count_changes(
      champion,
      "nerf",
      release_date + 1L,
      release_date + balance_window_days
    )
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, nerf_patches_6w_after := mapply(
  function(champion, release_date) {
    count_changes(
      champion,
      "nerf",
      release_date + 1L,
      release_date + balance_window_days,
      distinct_patches = TRUE
    )
  },
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]

Exclude releases close to champion releases or reworks

The base skin’s release date is the champion release date. A non-base skin launched on that date or during the next 60 days is excluded because newly released champions are generally less stable and always launch with at least one skin.

The confidence filter is unnecessary for reworks in the current database because every rework classification is already CERTAIN or VERY_CERTAIN. The exclusion nevertheless uses all rework labels so it remains conservative if the classifier is rerun later.

Code 
rework_dates <- unique(
  classified_changes[
    classification_label == "rework" & !is.na(effective_date),
    .(champion_id, effective_date)
  ]
)
reworks_by_champion <- split(as.integer(rework_dates$effective_date), rework_dates$champion_id)

has_nearby_rework <- function(champion, release_date) {
  dates <- reworks_by_champion[[as.character(champion)]]
  !is.null(dates) && any(abs(dates - as.integer(release_date)) <= rework_window_days)
}

skin_windows[, excluded_for_rework := mapply(
  has_nearby_rework,
  champion_id,
  skin_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, days_since_champion_release := as.integer(
  skin_release_date - champion_release_date
)]
skin_windows[, excluded_for_champion_release :=
  days_since_champion_release >= 0L &
  days_since_champion_release <= champion_release_window_days]
skin_windows[, complete_performance_window := complete.cases(
  win_rate_1m_before,
  win_rate_2w_after,
  popularity_1m_before,
  popularity_2w_after
)]

analysis_data <- skin_windows[
  !excluded_for_champion_release &
    !excluded_for_rework &
    complete_performance_window
]
analysis_data[, `:=`(
  win_rate_change = win_rate_2w_after - win_rate_1m_before,
  popularity_change = popularity_2w_after - popularity_1m_before,
  any_buff_6w_before = buff_entries_6w_before > 0L,
  any_nerf_6w_after = nerf_entries_6w_after > 0L,
  release_year = as.integer(format(skin_release_date, "%Y"))
)]
analysis_data[, popularity_percentile := frank(
  popularity_1m_before,
  ties.method = "average"
) / .N]
analysis_data[, popularity_quartile := cut(
  popularity_percentile,
  breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1),
  labels = c("Q1: least popular", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4: most popular"),
  include.lowest = TRUE
)]
setorder(analysis_data, skin_release_date, champion_name, skin_id)

cohort_flow <- data.table(

    "Dated, non-base, non-cancelled releases from 2011",
    "After excluding releases within 60 days of champion release",
    "After excluding releases within 60 days of a rework",
    "After requiring all four interpolated measurements"

  releases = c(
    nrow(skin_windows),
    skin_windows[excluded_for_champion_release == FALSE, .N],
    skin_windows[
      excluded_for_champion_release == FALSE & excluded_for_rework == FALSE,
      .N
    ],
    nrow(analysis_data)
  )
)

General buff and nerf statistics

The overall table covers every buff and nerf classification in the database regardless of whether a skin was released nearby. It reports both the complete classified counts and the high-confidence subset used by the analysis.

Code 
overall_balance_statistics <- classified_changes[
  classification_label %chin% c("buff", "nerf"),
  .(
    classified_entries = .N,
    confident_entries = sum(confidence %chin% accepted_confidence),
    confident_share = mean(confidence %chin% accepted_confidence),
    entries_with_known_date = sum(!is.na(effective_date)),
    champions = uniqueN(champion_id),
    distinct_patch_ids = uniqueN(patch_id)
  ),
  by = classification_label
]
setorder(overall_balance_statistics, classification_label)

Baseline by patch year

The yearly baseline is independent of skin releases. It uses patch effective dates and the same confidence threshold as the skin-window counts, making the annual buff/nerf comparison directly relevant to the later analysis. Entries whose Wiki history has no known effective date remain in the overall table above but cannot be assigned to a year.

Code 
general_balance_by_year_long <- classified_changes[
  classification_label %chin% c("buff", "nerf") & !is.na(effective_date),
  .(
    classified_entries = .N,
    confident_entries = sum(confidence %chin% accepted_confidence)
  ),
  by = .(
    patch_year = as.integer(format(effective_date, "%Y")),
    classification_label
  )
]
setorder(general_balance_by_year_long, patch_year, classification_label)

Counts in skin-release windows

These counts are conditional on the analysis cohort. Because windows can overlap—and because multiple skins can share a champion and release date—the totals are counts relative to skin releases rather than counts of unique underlying balance entries.

Code 
skin_window_balance_statistics <- rbindlist(list(
  analysis_data[, .(
    classification = "buff before release",
    total_entries = sum(buff_entries_6w_before),

Results by release year

Annual summaries help reveal whether a pooled relationship is driven by a particular period. Years before the graph history begins do not appear because the cohort requires both pre- and post-release performance measurements. The latest year may also be incomplete.

Interpretation and next modelling step

The plots describe what happens around skin releases and whether the descriptive pattern differs with pre-release popularity. They are not yet a causal test. Calendar time, champion-specific balancing frequency, repeated skins for the same champion, patch cadence, and general changes in Riot’s release practices can all confound the comparison.

A suitable next step is a matched case-control or event-study design. For each real release, sample control dates for the same champion from periods with sufficient graph coverage and no nearby skin or rework, then compare the probability or count of preceding buffs. Champion and calendar-period effects can subsequently be included in a conditional logistic, count, or mixed-effects model.
